label: Multiplayer Projects
title:
Work on projects.
Not alone.
subtitle: Invite teammates with a link, approve access requests, and share agent profiles, skills, and project files. See who is running what, and whose keys are paying for it.
summary: Invite your team into a project, share profiles and skills, and see whose keys pay for shared automation.
highlights: Any member creates an invite link; an owner or admin approves each request
Approved members join as admins and share profiles, skills, env vars, and library files
Every member’s chat sessions are visible, with a my sessions / all sessions filter
A Credential Attribution panel flags shared work running on a personal key, with a Fix link
Offboarding previews a departing member’s resources before they lose access

screenshots.caption: One project, every member’s sessions — switch between my sessions and all sessions

details.headline: Invite, request, approve
details.body: Any active member creates an invite link. The recipient opens it and requests access — an owner or admin approves before they join. Approved members join as admins, with full project control except deleting the project or transferring ownership.

screenshot.alt: Settings → Access showing an owner and four admins, two pending access requests (one GitHub verified, one flagged as having no repo access), and an invite link with its expiry, use count, and Copy, New Link, and Revoke controls
screenshot.caption: Members, pending requests, and the invite link — all managed from Settings → Access

details.headline: A request, not an automatic add
details.body: Sharing a link is safe: nobody joins your project until someone with permission approves them. SAM also checks whether the requester’s GitHub sign-in already has access to the linked repository, so approvers have context before deciding.

screenshot.alt: The Request Access card a recipient sees after opening a project invite link
screenshot.caption: Opening an invite link only creates a request — nobody joins automatically

details.headline: See everyone’s work, or just yours
details.body: Members share agent profiles, skills, project environment variables and secrets, and library files. A my sessions / all sessions filter on the chat list lets you focus on your own work or watch everything happening in the project.

screenshot.alt: Project chat with the All sessions filter selected, listing eight sessions started by five different team members, each labelled with who started it
screenshot.caption: Switch between my sessions and all sessions to see the whole project’s activity

details.headline: Know whose keys are paying
details.body: Personal API keys and cloud credentials always stay personal — a teammate’s trigger bills their key, not yours. The Credential Attribution panel lists triggers, tasks, nodes, and deployments running on a personal key, with a Fix link to move them onto a shared project credential.

screenshot.alt: Credential Attribution panel showing a trigger flagged as running on a personal key with a Fix link, next to resources covered by the project’s shared Hetzner credential
screenshot.caption: See at a glance which shared resources run on a personal key
